channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: When does a hybrid attack become an attack on NATO?
item.description: Two ships have been hit by drones in Bulgarian waters in the Black Sea on Monday. Several other ships have been targeted in recent weeks, at a time when Russia is intensifying its attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: [Financial Times] Ukraine blindsided by Starlink restrictions and intelligence gaps during Russian attack
item.description: Moscow ignores Donald Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ while Kyiv’s forces experience connectivity problems on Elon Musk’s satellite network

item.title: [Politico Europe] Budget ‘beerlaterals’: How Burnham and Healey really work
item.description: As President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrives in Downing Street, is the balance of the Ukraine war shifting? Andy Burnham will reaffirm Britain’s support for Ukraine after Presidents Trump and Putin reached a diesel deal – but can the UK still make a difference without putting its relationship with Washington at risk? Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Saudi Aramco HQ attacked in suspected Houthi strike
item.description: Iran-backed militants retaliate after Riyadh-led coalition targets sites in Yemen’s capital

item.title: [Financial Times] AI demand to exceed supply for 2 more years, says ASML
item.description: Europe’s most valuable company said its clients that include TSMC and Intel were experiencing ‘very, very strong demand’

item.title: [EU Observer] The ‘Transformative AI Strategy for Europe’ diagnoses the problem – but its solution is capitulation
item.description: Europe can only fully prepare for the AI transformation and maintain our sovereign control if the default action is to consider how can we use or create a European solution first, rather than capitulate to what Big Tech offers.

item.title: [Financial Times] Marine Le Pen vows ‘trial of strength’ with EU
item.description: Far-right leader aims for radical change in bloc’s powers and budget even as she tries to reassure voters over her pragmatism

item.title: [Financial Times] The art of living dangerously
item.description: It would be nice to think that the world will become less shock-prone, but it probably won’t

item.title: [Financial Times] How Ukraine’s data centre strikes threw Russia into turmoil
item.description: Kyiv’s attacks exposed vulnerabilities of Kremlin effort to centralise internet services under one company

item.title: [Financial Times] Military briefing: Houthis expose limits of Saudi Arabia’s vast arsenal
item.description: The kingdom is one of the world’s top arms buyers but has struggled to keep pace with the Iranian-backed rebels’ tactics

item.title: [Financial Times] CoreWeave targets ‘unlimited’ insurance money to fund AI build-out
item.description: Co-founder eyes insurers’ vast capital for loans as the Nvidia-backed cloud provider seeks to fund the data centre build-out

item.title: [Financial Times] How I used AI to become a chess grandmaster at 16
item.description: Ignore the doomsayers, this technology has transformed the game for the better and it can do the same for education

item.title: [Politico Europe] Europe’s development aid dilemma
item.description: The Commission is grappling with two goals that may be counterproductive: cutting migration and slashing development aid. The EU executive’s argument is that a slash in development funding will likely result in people showing up at European borders in search of a better life. And that’s a problem for the bloc, since it’s looking to […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Schaffe, schaffe, Rentenreform: Merz und sein neuer Arbeitsminister
item.description: Ein verschnupfter und heiser Kanzler im Angriffsmodus – wohl auch heute bei der Regierungserklärung am Nachmittag im Bundestag. Beim Arbeitgebertag gestern hat der Regierungschef Merz gut ausgeteilt und seinen neuen Arbeits- und Sozialminister Alexander Schweitzer öffentlich unter Druck gesetzt. Die Rentenreform soll im Eiltempo durchs Kabinett, doch in der SPD brodelt es gewaltig. Die Analyse […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine brings war effort to football’s Champions League
item.description: "It's a good time to invest in Ukraine, not from the point of view of big and easy money. It's a great time to invest from the view of strategic security issues," the club sponsor urged Europe.

item.title: [Politico Europe] How Europe can increase resilience to global shocks — live updates
item.description: Follow updates from inside the room at our European Resilience Summit, where we’re discussing how Europe can strengthen its ability to prosper in an increasingly fragmented world.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Corruption could become harder to catch under new EU budget, watchdog warns
item.description: Greater spending flexibility could make it harder to "follow the money,” said the chief of the European Court of Auditors.

item.title: [Financial Times] US arrests Saudi employee of OpenAI for allegedly bugging its offices
item.description: AI lab discovered a recording device concealed behind a television in a conference room

item.title: [Politico Europe] OpenAI employee arrested and charged over hidden recording
item.description: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, planted a sophisticated recording device in an OpenAI office, authorities said.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Burnham pledges ‘rock-solid support’ for Ukraine as Zelenskyy makes UK trip
item.description: The British leader has asked ministers to draw up proposals for further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to help the war-torn country.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
item.description: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
item.description: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president's decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
item.description: The new mantra? Don’t panic about owning the models — put them to work instead.

item.title: [EU Observer] Could Islamophobia one day become EU law?
item.description: An Islamophobic EU Parliament motion has showed that Europe's Muslims have reached an impossible crossroads - to integrate and forget their roots, or stay true to their traditions and risk being treated as a fifth column.

item.title: [Politico Europe] From no cards to many: Europe warns Trump not to waste Ukraine’s leverage
item.description: Ukraine's campaign against Russia's refineries is a growing problem for the U.S. president.

item.title: [EU Observer] Low pay and stress forcing Europe’s care workers to quit jobs, unions warn
item.description: Almost half of workers helping families care for children, older people, and people with disabilities in Europe have considered quitting due to low pay and bad working conditions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine killing record number of Russian troops, as Putin resorts to using gangs to boost enlistment (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,692)
item.description: Soaring Russian casualty rates and shrinking recruitment mean frontline units risk running out of men to hold or advance in Donbas, even as Ukraine keeps blowing up their supply trucks and fuel tankers.

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen pledges more cash for Egypt and Libya regimes to keep Sudanese genocide victims out of Europe
item.description: They fled genocide in Sudan to find persecution in Egypt so they moved on to Libya, but von der Leyen aims to pay Cairo and Tripoli to keep Sudanese refugees out of Fortress EU.

item.title: [EU Observer] Burnham to prioritise trade and migration at UK-EU summit, after accusing Russia of meddling in Brexit referendum
item.description: The UK-EU "status quo is not good enough for Britain", claimed the British prime minister after accusing Russia of meddling in the Brexit referendum.

item.title: [EU Observer] Socialist MEPs urge von der Leyen to cap methane-rules delay at one year, or withdraw it
item.description: In a letter sent on Monday to commission president von der Leyen, five centre-left MEPs said any postponement must be “strictly limited to a single year.”

item.title: [DW] Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
item.description: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

item.title: [EU Observer] Who ordered the strike that killed my friend and maimed me? The EU must demand answers from Israel
item.description: I survived an Israeli strike on 13 October 2023 with one leg missing, while my friend and colleague Issam was killed. Yet three years later, no one has been held accountable. I am asking the EU to turn its commitments to protecting journalists into concrete action: demand answers from Israel and use its leverage to ensure that those responsible face justice.

item.title: [DW] Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Could the EU shield the ICC from US sanctions?
item.description: The United States has imposed new sanctions on the International Criminal Court, this time targeting the institution itself. The EU, while supportive of the ICC, does little to counter the sanctions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Poll shows public revulsion on caged hens ahead of EU-ban deadline
item.description: In a poll of 25,080 adults across 25 EU member states, 75 percent of Europeans indicated support for a hen-cage ban by 2035.

item.title: [DW] What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
item.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s skills passport is missing a page, EMPASS wants to add it
item.description: Employers are reporting skills bottlenecks because CVs and qualifications often fail to capture skills they are looking for. Europe needs bridges between education and employment.

item.title: [DW] Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

item.title: [DW] Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

item.title: [DW] Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

item.title: [EU Observer] France, Greece, and Netherlands see steep fall in crisis-resilience, study finds
item.description: With one in five adults worldwide hit by disasters in the past five years, millions of people in Greece and France could be dangerously exposed when the next natural or man-made crisis strikes.

item.title: [DW] UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.

item.title: [DW] Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
item.description: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs don’t have to meekly accept an EU budget deal, but will they go to war over €141bn in cuts?
item.description: MEPs and the champions of EU integration point to the parliament's co-decision powers as proof of the institution's importance. But will MEPs dare use those powers in a budget fight with governments?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Spanish socialist MEP sees no other leader than Sánchez, as housing and immigration dominate snap election
item.description: Some 23 percent of Spain’s working population were immigrants, who were “paying taxes and [contributing to] pensions for everyone," said the MEP, ahead of a snap election dominated by its housing crisis and the Ceuta migrant crisis.

item.title: [DW] Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

item.title: [DW] Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

item.title: [DW] Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
item.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
item.description: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

item.title: [DW] Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?
